title: Thermal-aware instance mix & benchmarking heuristics
content:
Purpose: quick reference sheet for incorporating thermal behavior and power-capping into instance selection heuristics for cost-per-token recommendations.

Summary:
- We observed non-linear changes in tokens/sec when GPUs hit sustained power/thermal limits. Raw perf-per-dollar alone misleads when long steady-state runs are common.
- This sheet folds in (1) steady-state throttling factor, (2) perf/W measured in situ, and (3) simple $/token math to generate recommended instance mixes for steady vs bursty workloads.

Assumptions (baseline used for all rows):
- Batch size/sequence profile: typical chat workload, 32-token prompt + 128-token generation average (approx 160 tokens total), 80% short, 20% long (>=1024).
- Measurements run on CUDA driver 12.x, cuDNN 9.x, kernel patches applied (bench harness v0.9).
- Currency: USD. Cloud list price used for price/hr (pre-commit discounts).

Reference formulas (apply to each measured row):
- tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $/token = price_per_hour / tokens_per_hour
- perf_per_watt = tokens_per_sec / average_gpu_power_watts
- throttled_tokens_per_sec = tokens_per_sec * (1 - throttling_penalty)

Benchmark table (steady-state throughput tests, 16-bit and 4-bit runs where applicable):
Columns: Instance | GPU | price_hr | measured_tokens_sec | avg_gpu_power_w | throttling_penalty | throttled_tps | $/token (steady) | perf/W (tokens/sec/W) | notes
A10-Standard | A10 | 0.86 | 240 | 95 | 0.06 | 225.6 | 0.0000107 | 2.53 | good for short-context, power efficient at low SLOs
L4-Std | L4 | 1.10 | 410 | 115 | 0.03 | 397.7 | 0.0000070 | 3.56 | strong mid-range burst; quantized 4-bit gives +18% tokens/sec
A100-40GB | A100 | 3.50 | 980 | 320 | 0.12 | 862.4 | 0.0000104 | 3.06 | high throughput but heavy throttling on long sequences unless power cap tuned
H100-80GB | H100 | 5.20 | 1240 | 360 | 0.18 | 1016.8 | 0.0000115 | 3.44 | best tail latency, highest raw perf; subject to rack-level thermal limits

Notes on table numbers and methodology:
- price_hr: sample public on-demand list prices for comparable cloud instances (rounded). Use committed discounts for final pricing.
- measured_tokens_sec: median observed tokens/sec over a 30m steady generation run (not microbursts).
- avg_gpu_power_w: average GPU package power measured via nvidia-smi sampling at 5s cadence during the run.
- throttling_penalty: percent loss due to thermal slowdown or pstate/powercap enforcement (derived from comparing first-2min vs last-10min throughput).
- $/token computed using throttled_tokens_per_sec (steady-state economics).

Heuristics and actionable rules (for runtime routing and recommendations):
1) If median request length < 200 tokens and P95 tail < 512, prioritize L4 for cost-sensitive routes (lower $/token after quantization).
2) For long-run batch scoring or embedding-heavy workloads (sustained >10m continuous generation), apply a throttling multiplier: effective_tokens = measured_tokens_sec * (1 - throttling_penalty). Evaluate A100 with tuned powercap if throttling_penalty > 0.1.
3) Use perf/W as a tie-breaker when unit price/hr differences are <20%. Prefer instance with higher perf/W to reduce infrastructure power budget and cooling footprint.
4) For SLA-sensitive routes (p95 latency target), prefer H100 variants but consider burst buffer on L4 for occasional spikes to reduce cost.

Instance-mix quick recommendations (initial guess for capacity planners):
- Latency-sensitive product API (steady 200 rps, avg tokens 80): 60% L4, 30% H100 (canary), 10% A100 reserved for nightly large-batch fallbacks.
- High-throughput batch scoring (single-shots >1024 tokens): 80% A100, 20% H100 for tail isolation (ensure powercap tuning).
- Cost-first chatbots (mostly short convos): 90% L4, 10% A10 for dev/noncritical traffic.

Sensitivity checks to run (recommended bench jobs):
- Vary ambient rack temp +10C to see thermal penalty shifts (simulate colder/hotter DC zones).
- Run with powercap at 95%, 90%, 85% (observe tokens/sec delta) to find sweet spot where perf/W improves but $/token doesn't meaningfully increase.
- Quantization sensitivity: compare 16->8->4-bit throughput and quality delta using curated eval prompts (linked).

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Validate A10 numbers on A10X variant (some providers have different thermal envelopes). (Owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Add tail-latency microburst sheet that pairs per-route burst mix to autoscaling cost curve. (Owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Run a 24h steady-state job across a zone to capture multi-hour thermal drift (ticket JIRA-OPT-1345).
- [ ] Confirm list vs committed pricing delta and add one-click multiplier for committed contracts. (Owner: Priya)

Linked experiments and artifacts:
- bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (see run-config thermal-experiment-2025-02)
- logs: s3://redwood-bench/thermal/2025-02-14/ (performance traces and nvidia-smi dumps)
- eval set: confluence.redwood/opt/quant-evals/top-1000-chat-prompts

Short checklist for converting this draft into a canonical sheet: 
- import these measured rows into the canonical token-econ sheet -> add committed-price layer and region multipliers.
- Add a column for effective rack cooling cost (est $/kWh amortized) to reflect perf/W economics at infra level.
- Run tuning experiments on powercap for the A100/H100 runs and re-calc throttling_penalty.

Audience notes: This is a working draft targeted at product and infra owners who need heuristics to recommend instance families to customers and to build autoscaling policies in Redwood Optimize. Treat numbers as experimental until the 24h runs complete.
